In `r last_full` the highest-rated team outside the resume top 25 is `r dis$team`: power rank `r dis$power_rank` (`r fmt(dis$power, 1)` points) but resume rank `r dis$resume_rank`, at `r dis$wins`--`r dis$losses`. @tbl-dis-example shows why, game by game. Its own posterior gave it an expected `r fmt(dis$xwins, 1)` wins against this schedule, so its win luck is `r fmt(dis$luck, 1)`; `r nrow(dis_losses)` losses, `r sum(abs(dis_losses$pf - dis_losses$pa) <= 8)` of them by one score, cost it `r fmt(-sum(dis_losses$wab_game), 2)` wins of $\WAB$, while its `r sum(dis_games$W)` wins earned `r fmt(sum(dis_games$wab_game[dis_games$W == 1]), 2)`. The power rating reads those losses as close games that a strong team loses sometimes; the resume counts them as losses.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dis-example
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Resume against power, game by game, for ", dis$team, " in ", last_full, ". $p_g$: the team''s own win probability under the final posterior; $\\bar\\pi_g$: the benchmark''s.")'
dis_games |>
  transmute(Week = week_label, Opponent = gsub("&", "\\&", opp, fixed = TRUE), Score = paste0(pf, "--", pa),
            `$p_g$` = fmt(p_win, 2), `$\\bar\\pi_g$` = fmt(p_bench, 2), `$W_g - \\bar\\pi_g$` = fmt(wab_game, 2)) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrr")
```

## The `r last_full` Playoff Field {#sec-cfp}

```{r}
cfp_teams <- g_last |> filter(season_type == "postseason", grepl("College Football Playoff", notes))
field_ids <- unique(c(cfp_teams$home_id, cfp_teams$away_id))
cfp_week <- max(ratings$week[ratings$season == last_full & !is.na(ratings$cfp_rank)])
pre25 <- ratings |> filter(season == last_full, week == cfp_week, tier == 1)
field_tab <- pre25 |> filter(team_id %in% field_ids | resume_rank <= 12 | cfp_rank <= 12) |>
  mutate(in_field = team_id %in% field_ids) |>
  arrange(coalesce(cfp_rank, 99L), resume_rank)
out_model <- field_tab |> filter(!in_field, resume_rank <= 12)
in_not_model <- field_tab |> filter(in_field, resume_rank > 12)
```

The first question a reader will ask of a resume is whether it picks the teams the committee picked. @tbl-cfp compares the `r last_full` playoff field with the model at the committee's final ranking (the posterior through the conference championships, week `r cfp_week`). The resume's top 12 contains `r sum(field_tab$in_field & field_tab$resume_rank <= 12)` of the `r length(field_ids)` teams in the field. `r if (nrow(in_not_model)) paste0("In the field but outside the resume top 12: ", paste0(in_not_model$team, " (resume ", in_not_model$resume_rank, ", CFP ", in_not_model$cfp_rank, ")", collapse = "; "), ". ") else ""``r if (nrow(out_model)) paste0("In the resume top 12 but not in the field: ", paste0(out_model$team, " (resume ", out_model$resume_rank, ", CFP ", ifelse(is.na(out_model$cfp_rank), "unranked", out_model$cfp_rank), ")", collapse = "; "), ".") else ""` The field is not simply the committee's top 12: the five highest-ranked conference champions qualify automatically, which is how a team outside the top 12 of any ranking can be selected.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cfp
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("The ", last_full, " playoff field and the model at the committee''s final ranking. Teams in the field, in the resume top 12, or in the committee''s top 12. Field: selected for the playoff.")'
field_tab |>
  transmute(Team = gsub("&", "\\&", team, fixed = TRUE), Record = paste0(wins, "--", losses),
            Field = ifelse(in_field, "yes", ""), CFP = ifelse(is.na(cfp_rank), "--", cfp_rank),
            Resume = resume_rank, `$\\WAB$` = fmt(wab, 2), SOR = sor_prob |> signif(2) |> format(),
            Power = power_rank, AP = ifelse(is.na(ap_rank), "--", ap_rank)) |>
  ktab(align = "llcrrrrrr")
```

## The Resume Against the Committee {#sec-validate-resume}

A retrodictive ranking has no future outcome to score it against, so the evidence for the resume has to be external. @tbl-committee compares each ranking with the committee's final ranking in every season since the playoff began: overlap with the playoff field (the top four through 2023, the twelve selected teams since 2024), with the committee's top 4 and top 12, and the rank correlation over the committee's 25. It also reports retrodictive accuracy: the share of the season's FBS--FBS games whose winner the final ranking places higher. The legacy composite that this model replaced is not included, because its code was retired with the defects listed in the project plan and cannot be rerun on the same data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-committee
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Rankings against the committee, ", min(rv$committee$season), "--", max(rv$committee$season), " (mean over seasons), at the snapshot before the committee''s final ranking, and retrodictive accuracy at the end of each season. SOR ranks teams by strength of record.")'
rv$committee |>
  group_by(system) |>
  summarise(field = mean(field_overlap / n_field), top4 = mean(top4_overlap), top12 = mean(top12_overlap),
            rho = mean(rho_cfp25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(rv$retro |> group_by(system) |> summarise(retro = weighted.mean(retro_acc, games), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "system") |>
  mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("Resume", "SOR", "Colley", "Power", "AP"))) |>
  arrange(system) |>
  transmute(Ranking = as.character(system), `Field overlap` = pct(field), `Top 4 (of 4)` = fmt(top4, 2),
            `Top 12 (of 12)` = fmt(top12, 1), `$\\rho$, CFP top 25` = fmt(rho, 2),
            `Retrodictive accuracy` = ifelse(is.na(retro), "--", pct(retro, 1))) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrr")
cm <- rv$committee |> group_by(system) |> summarise(field = mean(field_overlap / n_field), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
rt_acc <- rv$retro |> group_by(system) |> summarise(a = weighted.mean(retro_acc, games), .groups = "drop")
ra <- setNames(rt_acc$a, rt_acc$system)
```

`r if (cm$system[which.max(cm$field)] == "AP") "The AP poll agrees with the committee most closely, which is unsurprising: both are made by people watching the same games, and the poll is known to the committee. " else ""`Among the computer rankings the resume and SOR match the committee's field in `r pct(cm$field[cm$system == "Resume"])` and `r pct(cm$field[cm$system == "SOR"])` of places, Colley in `r pct(cm$field[cm$system == "Colley"])` and the power rating in `r pct(cm$field[cm$system == "Power"])`. `r if (min(cm$field[cm$system %in% c("Resume", "SOR")]) > cm$field[cm$system == "Power"]) "The committee selects on results, as the resume does, more than on strength." else "The committee's field is no closer to the resume than to the power rating."` Retrodictive accuracy is `r pct(ra[["Resume"]], 1)` for the resume, `r pct(ra[["SOR"]], 1)` for SOR, `r pct(ra[["Colley"]], 1)` for Colley and `r pct(ra[["Power"]], 1)` for power`r if (ra[["Power"]] < min(ra[c("Resume", "SOR", "Colley")])) ": a ranking built from the record explains the record better than one built to predict" else ""`.


# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The design principle of this paper is that a ranking should say which question it answers, and that different questions can share a model without sharing a formula. The power rating and the resume come from one posterior and are never mixed: the resume borrows the model's estimate of how hard each game was, and nothing else. That separation has a cost --- two numbers where the public expects one --- but each number can then be checked against something observable: the power rating against future games (@sec-backtest), and the resume, less directly, against the committee's selections and the season's own results (@sec-validate-resume).

**Limitations.** Several choices deserve more work.

1. *The margin distribution near zero.* The model underpredicts one-score games in `r n_w7_fail` of `r nrow(w7)` seasons (@sec-ppc), and neither a two-normal scale mixture nor a scale that grows with the mismatch removes the misfit, although the latter improves the LOO density considerably (@sec-family). The remaining reason is that margins are integers with spikes at key numbers (3 and 7) and at zero (overtime games, whose regulation margin is zero by construction), while the likelihood is continuous. This affects spread and cover probabilities rather than win probabilities. Alternatives that respect the discreteness are models for the two scores themselves, such as the bivariate Poisson of @karlisAnalysisSportsData2003 or the hierarchical score model of @baioBayesianHierarchicalModel2010, or a rounded (interval-censored) version of the present likelihood. They should be compared on the margin's LOO density.
2. *One step size for every team and week.* The random walk of @eq-walk moves every team by Gaussian steps of the same size, so a team that loses its quarterback in October is pulled down only gradually, at the rate the whole sport's drift allows, and a slow decline and a sudden one look alike. Heavier-tailed steps, or a step size that varies by team or by part of the season, would let a rating jump; the data identify even one step size only weakly (@sec-hierarchy), so such extensions would need informative structure, such as injury reports, rather than more parameters alone.
3. *Asymmetric garbage time.* The efficiency margin excludes garbage time (the provider's definition), but the scoreboard margin cannot: a team that leads by 30 and rests its starters concedes late points that enter $y_g$ but not $e_g$. That shrinks the scoreboard margin of lopsided games relative to their efficiency margin, which the model can only absorb in $\lambda$ (the efficiency scale per point of margin) and $\kappa$; both are therefore averages over close and lopsided games. A margin-dependent $\lambda$, or a garbage-time-filtered scoreboard margin, would separate the two.
4. *Priors from the whole history.* The structural priors use every complete season (@sec-priors), weighted towards the recent ones. The leave-one-season-out comparisons of @sec-loso bound what that borrows; a strictly prospective version would set each season's priors from earlier seasons only. The preseason terms use only two team-level roster numbers; player-level returning production, incoming transfers and coaching staffs would sharpen the first weeks further, where the model still trails the market most (@sec-bt-accuracy).
5. *A simple total model.* Offence and defence come from a total model that is Gaussian, independent of the margin given the ratings, and blind to the score of overtime games (@sec-total). It trails the closing over/under (@sec-bt-accuracy), and the priors of the total model and of the random-walk steps are provisional: they were set from preliminary fits rather than pooled from the vague-prior refits as the other structural priors were, and the twelve pooled priors themselves date from the static Student-$t$ model (@sec-priors). Re-pooling all of them under the published model is the next step.
6. *Games are exchangeable.* Motivation, rest, travel, injuries and weather are all absent, and home field is one number per season for every venue (@fig-hfa); the gap to the closing line in @sec-backtest is a measure of how much they matter.

```{r, supp-setup}
col_fit <- c(first = col_ref, final = col_ink)

# Parameter names as plotmath, for facet strips (label_parsed). The figures show the margin

pm_all <- c(
```

# Appendix: Supplementary Posterior Checks {#sec-supp .appendix}

The weekly posteriors of @sec-computation are checked by gates and summaries only, because keeping every draw of `r n_snap` fits is not needed for publication. This appendix examines two posteriors in full, following the checklist of @kahleOverviewBayesianComputation2022 and @miyakawaPracticalComparisonBayesian2025 for applied Bayesian computation --- sampler behaviour; convergence (smooth, chain-consistent marginal densities, well-mixed traces, quickly damping autocorrelation, a Gelman--Rubin statistic approaching one); posterior geometry; the justification of informative priors and the priors they induce on derived quantities; sensitivity of the posterior to changes in the prior; predictive adequacy; and influence --- together with the visual workflow of @gabryVisualizationBayesianWorkflow2019. The two posteriors bracket the range the pipeline fits:

- **`r fit_lab[["first"]]`**: `r fmt(nrow(sup$first$played))` games, about one per team. The data barely constrain a team's strength, the hierarchy and the carry-over do most of the work, and this is where the hierarchical geometry is hardest for the sampler.
- **`r fit_lab[["final"]]`**: all `r fmt(nrow(sup$final$played))` games of the season, including the postseason.

Both are refitted with the production settings of @sec-gates (`r n_chains` chains, `r fmt(S_draws / n_chains)` post-warm-up draws each, `r fmt(S_draws)` in all) by the `supplement` target in `R/06_supplement.R`.

## Sampler Behaviour Across All Snapshots {#sec-supp-all}

Before the two detailed fits, @fig-supp-gates shows the gate statistics of every weekly posterior. The retry of @sec-gates is visible as the fits with doubled sampling.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-gates
#| fig-cap: "Gate statistics of all weekly posteriors by week, every season overlaid. Left: the largest rank-normalised $\\widehat R$ over all monitored parameters, with the gate at 1.01. Centre: the smallest bulk or tail effective sample size, with the gate at 400. Right: wall-clock time of the fit, four chains in parallel. Filled points are fits that needed the retry."
#| fig-scap: "Gate statistics of every weekly posterior"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.36
params |>
  transmute(week, retry = attempts > 1, `Max R-hat` = max_rhat,
            `Min ESS` = pmin(min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail), `Seconds` = seconds) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Max R-hat`, `Min ESS`, Seconds)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Seconds"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, value)) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(name = factor(c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS"), levels = c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Seconds")),
                           g = c(cfg$gates$rhat, cfg$gates$ess)),
             aes(yintercept = g), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = retry), size = 1.2, colour = col_ink, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 19), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week", y = NULL)
```

## Sampler Diagnostics {#sec-supp-sampler}

@tbl-supp-sampler reports the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo diagnostics of each chain [@betancourtConceptualIntroductionHamiltonian2017]: the adapted step size, the mean number of leapfrog steps per iteration, how often the trajectory hit the maximum tree depth (which would indicate a truncated, inefficient exploration), divergent transitions (which indicate curvature the integrator cannot follow and a potentially biased posterior), and the energy Bayesian fraction of missing information, E-BFMI [@betancourtDiagnosingSuboptimalCotangent2016].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-sampler
#| tbl-cap: "Sampler diagnostics by chain. E-BFMI below 0.2 would indicate that the momentum resampling cannot move the chain across energy levels fast enough; the maximum tree depth is 10."
ebfmi <- function(E) sum(diff(E)^2) / sum((E - mean(E))^2)
sampler_tab <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  tm <- fit$time$chains
  d |>
    group_by(Chain = .chain) |>
    summarise(`Step size` = fmt(mean(stepsize__), 3),
              `Leapfrog steps` = fmt(mean(n_leapfrog__), 1),
              `Max depth` = max(treedepth__),
              `At max depth` = sum(treedepth__ >= fit$metadata$max_treedepth),
              Divergent = sum(divergent__),
              `E-BFMI` = fmt(ebfmi(energy__), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(`Warm-up (s)` = fmt(tm$warmup, 1), `Sampling (s)` = fmt(tm$sampling, 1),
           Fit = ifelse(Chain == 1, fit_lab[[nm]], "")) |>
    select(Fit, Chain, everything())
})
sampler_tab |> ktab(align = "lrrrrrrrrr")
div_total <- sum(sampler_tab$Divergent)
maxdepth_total <- sum(sampler_tab$`At max depth`)
ebfmi_min <- min(as.numeric(sampler_tab$`E-BFMI`))
```

Neither fit has `r if (div_total == 0) "a single divergent transition" else paste(div_total, "divergent transitions")`, `r if (maxdepth_total == 0) "no iteration reaches" else paste(maxdepth_total, "iterations reach")` the maximum tree depth, and the smallest E-BFMI is `r fmt(ebfmi_min, 2)`, far above 0.2. The week-1 fit, with few data, needs no longer trajectories than the final one: the non-centred hierarchy keeps its geometry close to a product of normals.

@fig-supp-energy compares the marginal energy distribution with the distribution of energy changes between iterations. When the second is much narrower than the first, the sampler explores the energy levels of the posterior slowly and tails may be under-sampled; overlapping histograms are what a healthy fit looks like.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-energy
#| fig-cap: "Energy diagnostic. Grey: marginal energy $E$, centred; orange: the change in energy between successive iterations, $\\Delta E$. Pooled over chains."
#| fig-scap: "HMC energy diagnostic"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.34
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble() |>
    group_by(.chain) |>
    mutate(`E (centred)` = energy__ - mean(energy__), `Delta E` = c(NA, diff(energy__))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(`E (centred)`, `Delta E`) |>
    pivot_longer(everything()) |>
    mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = name)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`E (centred)` = col_ref, `Delta E` = col_power)) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

## Convergence {#sec-supp-convergence}

@tbl-supp-conv gives posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics of the structural parameters: the rank-normalised split-$\widehat R$, which compares between- and within-chain variation after rank-normalising and folding the draws [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992; @vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021]; bulk and tail effective sample sizes, which account for autocorrelation [@geyerPracticalMarkovChain1992]; and the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-conv
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics for the structural parameters of the margin model, the random-walk step and the family's shape parameters. \\emph{MCSE} is the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean. The total model's parameters are summarised in the text."
conv <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(
    fit$par, "mean", "sd",
    q5 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.05, names = FALSE), q95 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.95, names = FALSE),
    "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "mcse_mean"
  ) |> mutate(fit = nm)
})
conv |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab))) |>
  arrange(factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), variable) |>
  mutate(variable = as.character(variable)) |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(variable == names(pm_lab)[1], fit_lab[fit], ""),
         Parameter = tex_lab[variable],
         across(c(mean, sd, q5, q95), \(x) fmt(x, 2)),
         `$\\widehat R$` = fmt(rhat, 3), `ESS bulk` = fmt(ess_bulk), `ESS tail` = fmt(ess_tail),
         MCSE = fmt(mcse_mean, 3)) |>
  select(Fit, Parameter, Mean = mean, SD = sd, `5\\%` = q5, `95\\%` = q95,
         `$\\widehat R$`, `ESS bulk`, `ESS tail`, MCSE) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
worst <- conv |> slice_min(ess_bulk, n = 1)
conv_tot <- conv |> filter(variable %in% total_vars)
mcse_ratio <- max(conv$mcse_mean / conv$sd)
```

Every structural $\widehat R$, including those of the `r n_distinct(conv_tot$variable)` total-model parameters, is at most `r fmt(max(conv$rhat), 3)`, and the smallest bulk effective sample size is `r fmt(worst$ess_bulk)`, for `r sym_list(worst$variable)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[worst$fit]]))` fit`r if (nrow(conv_tot)) paste0(" (smallest among the total model's: ", fmt(min(conv_tot$ess_bulk)), ")") else ""`. `r if (worst$variable == "sigma_conf") "The conference spread $\\omega$ mixes most slowly: it is informed only by the forty-odd conference means, and its posterior is correlated with all of them. " else if (worst$variable == "tau_r") "The random-walk step $\\phi_r$ mixes most slowly: the data inform it only weakly, and its posterior is correlated with every step of every team (@sec-hierarchy). " else ""`Monte Carlo standard errors are at most `r pct(mcse_ratio, 1)` of the posterior standard deviations.

The team strengths are too many to tabulate. @fig-supp-rhat-ess shows the distribution of their $\widehat R$ and of their bulk effective sample size as a fraction of the number of draws.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-rhat-ess
#| fig-cap: "Convergence of all team strengths $r_i$. Left: rank-normalised $\\widehat R$, with the gate at 1.01. Right: bulk effective sample size per draw; values above one are possible for anti-correlated chains, which NUTS often produces for well-identified parameters."
#| fig-scap: "Convergence of all team strengths"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.36
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(fit$r, "rhat", "ess_bulk") |>
    transmute(`R-hat` = rhat, `Bulk ESS / draws` = ess_bulk / S_draws, fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  pivot_longer(-fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = fit)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(name = "R-hat", g = cfg$gates$rhat), aes(xintercept = g),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Teams")
```

Trace plots (@fig-supp-trace-final, @fig-supp-trace-first) show the chains iteration by iteration; well-mixed chains overlap and look like stationary noise, with no trends, no stuck stretches and no chain wandering off on its own. Rank plots (@fig-supp-rank) are more sensitive: the draws of all chains are ranked together, and if the chains sample the same distribution each chain's ranks are uniform [@vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021]. Kernel density estimates of each chain's marginal (@fig-supp-dens-chain) should be smooth, unimodal where the model implies it, and indistinguishable between chains. Autocorrelation (@fig-supp-acf) should damp quickly with the lag, since it determines the effective sample size. Finally, the Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (@fig-supp-gr) should fall to 1 as the chains lengthen and stay there [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992].

```{r}
trace_plot <- function(fit) {
  par_long(fit) |>
    ggplot(aes(.iteration, value, colour = factor(.chain))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = chain_greys, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
    labs(x = "Iteration (post-warm-up)", y = NULL)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-trace-final
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Trace plots of the structural parameters, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". One shade of grey per chain.")'
#| fig-scap: "Trace plots, final fit"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
trace_plot(sup$final)
```


```{r}

#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Rank plots of the structural parameters for both fits. For each parameter the draws of all chains are ranked jointly and each chain''s ranks are binned into 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. Lines are chains; ", fit_lab[["first"]], " in orange, ", fit_lab[["final"]], " in grey.")'
#| fig-scap: "Rank plots"

nb <- 20
per_bin <- S_draws / n_chains / nb
band <- qbinom(c(0.025, 0.975), S_draws / n_chains, 1 / nb)
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {

    group_by(variable) |>

}) |>

  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = nb + 0.5, ymin = band[1], ymax = band[2], fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.6) +

  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-dens-chain
#| fig-cap: "Kernel density estimates of each structural parameter's marginal posterior, one line per chain. Orange: week 1; grey: final. Chains that agree give overlapping curves; a bumpy or multimodal curve, or one chain apart from the others, would indicate poor exploration."
#| fig-scap: "Chain-wise marginal posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = nm)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, group = interaction(.chain, fit), colour = fit)) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-acf
#| fig-cap: "Autocorrelation of the structural parameters up to lag 20, averaged over chains. Orange: week 1; grey: final."
#| fig-scap: "Autocorrelation"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.8
acf_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  par_long(fit) |>
    group_by(variable, .chain) |>
    reframe(lag = 0:20, acf = as.numeric(stats::acf(value, lag.max = 20, plot = FALSE)$acf)) |>
    group_by(variable, lag) |>
    summarise(acf = mean(acf), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(fit = nm)
})
acf_df |>
  ggplot(aes(lag, acf, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) + geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = "Lag", y = "Autocorrelation")
# First lag at which the chain-averaged autocorrelation drops below 0.1
damp <- acf_df |>
  group_by(fit, variable) |>
  summarise(lag10 = suppressWarnings(min(lag[abs(acf) < 0.1])), .groups = "drop")
slow <- damp |> slice_max(lag10, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
slow_var <- names(pm_lab)[match(as.character(slow$variable), pm_lab)]
n_fast <- sum(damp$lag10 <= 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-gr
#| fig-cap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (rank-normalised split-$\\widehat R$) of each structural parameter computed on the first $n$ post-warm-up iterations of every chain, as $n$ grows. The dashed line is the gate at 1.01."
#| fig-scap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor against iteration"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
gr_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  arr <- fit$par
  ns <- unique(round(seq(50, posterior::niterations(arr), length.out = 25)))
  map_dfr(ns, function(n) {
    sub_arr <- posterior::subset_draws(arr, iteration = seq_len(n))
    tibble(n = n, variable = posterior::variables(arr),
           rhat = map_dbl(posterior::variables(arr), \(v) posterior::rhat(posterior::extract_variable_array(sub_arr, v))))
  }) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
})
gr_df |>
  ggplot(aes(n, rhat, group = variable)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cfg$gates$rhat, linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  geom_line(colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~fit) +
  labs(x = "Iterations per chain", y = expression(hat(R)))
gr_first_ok <- gr_df |> group_by(fit, n) |> summarise(m = max(rhat), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(fit) |> summarise(n_ok = min(n[m <= cfg$gates$rhat]), .groups = "drop")
```

The autocorrelation of `r n_fast` of the `r nrow(damp)` parameter--fit pairs drops below 0.1 within three lags; the slowest is `r sym_list(slow_var)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[slow$fit]]))` fit, which needs `r slow$lag10` lags, and even there the effective sample size is well above the gate. The shrink factors of every parameter are below the gate after `r fmt(max(gr_first_ok$n_ok))` iterations per chain in both fits and stay there, so the `r fmt(S_draws / n_chains)` iterations used are more than enough.

## Posterior Geometry {#sec-supp-geometry}

Hierarchical models have funnels: when a scale parameter such as $\omega$ or $\tau_1$ is small, the group effects it governs must be close to their mean, and the posterior narrows into a region the sampler can struggle to enter. The non-centred parameterisation of @eq-hier removes the funnel from the sampled coordinates when the data are weak [@papaspiliopoulosGeneralFrameworkParametrization2007]. @fig-supp-pairs plots each scale against a standardised effect it governs, in the sampled coordinates; divergent transitions, if any, would be drawn in orange and would typically concentrate at the neck of a funnel.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pairs
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Posterior geometry in the sampled coordinates, 1,000 draws per panel. Each panel plots the log of a scale parameter against a standardised effect it governs: the conference effect $u_c$ of the first FBS conference against $\\log\\omega$, and the team effect $z_i$ of the FBS team with the fewest games against $\\log\\tau_1$. Divergent transitions would be orange.")'
#| fig-scap: "Posterior geometry of the hierarchical scales"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.62
geom_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  p <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$par) |> as_tibble()
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  cr <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$conf_raw))
  zz <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$z))
  fbs_conf <- which(fit$conf_tier == 1L)[1]
  gp <- table(factor(c(fit$played$home, fit$played$away), levels = seq_len(nrow(fit$teams))))
  fbs_team <- which(fit$teams$tier == 1L)[which.min(gp[fit$teams$tier == 1L])]
  set.seed(1)
  keep <- sample.int(nrow(p), 1000)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(x = cr[keep, fbs_conf], y = log(p$sigma_conf[keep]), panel = "log(omega) ~ u[c]"),
    tibble(x = zz[keep, fbs_team], y = log(p$`sigma_team[1]`[keep]), panel = "log(tau[1]) ~ z[i]")
  ) |>
    mutate(div = rep(d$divergent__[keep], 2) == 1, fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
})
geom_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = div), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_ink, `TRUE` = col_power), guide = "none") +
  facet_grid(fit ~ panel, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(panel = label_parsed)) +
  labs(x = "Standardised effect", y = "Log scale")
```

Neither fit shows a funnel in the sampled coordinates: the standardised effects have the same spread at every value of the scale, which is the purpose of the non-centred parameterisation. In the final fit the team effect is nearly uncorrelated with $\tau_1$ and concentrated, because a full season pins the team down; in week 1 it spreads over its $\mathcal N(0, 1)$ prior, as it should with one game. The random walk has a funnel of the same kind, between the step $\phi_r$ and the standardised steps $\varepsilon_{i,k}$ of @eq-walk, which is not drawn because the steps are not kept; the evidence that the sampler enters its neck is the absence of divergent transitions, which the gates require of every published fit (@sec-gates), together with the informative prior that keeps $\phi_r$ away from zero.

## Prior and Posterior {#sec-supp-prior}

@fig-supp-prior-post overlays the prior density of each structural parameter on its posterior in both fits. The comparison shows what the data teach: in week 1 many posteriors stay close to the prior, which is why the priors of @sec-priors were set empirically, while by the end of the season most have contracted well inside it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-prior-post
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Prior (dashed) and posterior densities of the structural parameters. Priors are normal, truncated to the parameter''s support", if (has_nu) paste0(", except $\\nu \\sim \\mathrm{Gamma}(", cfg$nu_prior[1], ", ", cfg$nu_prior[2], ")$ on $\\nu > ", cfg$nu_lower, "$") else "", if (fam == "mixture") paste0(" and $p_w \\sim \\mathrm{Beta}(", cfg$p_wide_prior[1], ", ", cfg$p_wide_prior[2], ")$; $\\sigma_w$, whose prior is on $\\sigma_w - \\sigma_m$, has no curve") else "", ".")'
#| fig-scap: "Prior and posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 1.05
prior_spec <- pri |>
  mutate(dist = "normal") |>
  bind_rows(tibble(variable = c("nu", "p_wide", "gamma_m", "tau_r"), dist = c("gamma", "beta", "normal", "normal"),
                   mean = c(cfg$nu_prior[1], cfg$p_wide_prior[1], cfg$gamma_prior[1], cfg$tau_r_prior[1]),
                   sd = c(cfg$nu_prior[2], cfg$p_wide_prior[2], cfg$gamma_prior[2], cfg$tau_r_prior[2]))) |>
  # for the gamma and beta priors, mean and sd hold the two shape parameters
  mutate(lower = case_when(variable %in% c("hfa", "mu_tier[2]", "mu_tier[3]", "kappa") ~ -Inf,
                           variable == "nu" ~ cfg$nu_lower, TRUE ~ 0),
         upper = ifelse(variable %in% c("b_prev", "p_wide"), 1, Inf)) |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab))
prior_dens <- function(x, dist, a, b, lower, upper) {
  switch(dist,
    gamma = ifelse(x > lower, dgamma(x, a, b) / pgamma(lower, a, b, lower.tail = FALSE), 0),
    beta = dbeta(x, a, b),
    normal = ifelse(x > lower & x < upper, dnorm(x, a, b) / (pnorm(upper, a, b) - pnorm(lower, a, b)), 0))
}
post_long <- imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]]))
rng <- post_long |> group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.0005), hi = quantile(value, 0.9995), .groups = "drop")
prior_curves <- prior_spec |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab)) |>
  inner_join(rng, by = "variable") |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(variable = variable, {
    x <- seq(lo - 0.15 * (hi - lo), hi + 0.15 * (hi - lo), length.out = 300)
    tibble(x = x, dens = prior_dens(x, dist, mean, sd, lower, upper))
  })
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = post_long, aes(value, fill = fit, colour = fit), alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3, adjust = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = prior_curves, aes(x, dens), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) + scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

@fig-supp-contraction condenses the same comparison into two numbers per parameter [@schadPrincipledBayesianWorkflow2021]: the posterior contraction $1 - \Var_{\text{post}}/\Var_{\text{prior}}$, near one when the data dominate the prior, and the posterior $z$-score $(\E_{\text{post}} - \E_{\text{prior}})/\mathrm{sd}_{\text{post}}$, large in magnitude when the posterior sits far from where the prior expected it. Contraction near one with small $|z|$ is the ideal; high contraction with large $|z|$ indicates a prior--data conflict; low contraction indicates that the prior, not the data, is determining the answer.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-contraction
#| fig-cap: "Posterior contraction against posterior $z$-score for the structural parameters, for both fits. Prior moments are those of the truncated priors."
#| fig-scap: "Posterior contraction and z-scores"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
tn_moments <- function(m, s, a, b, dist = "normal") {
  if (dist == "gamma") {  # Gamma(m, s) truncated to (a, Inf), by numerical integration
    k <- pgamma(a, m, s, lower.tail = FALSE)
    m1 <- integrate(\(x) x * dgamma(x, m, s), a, Inf)$value / k
    m2 <- integrate(\(x) x^2 * dgamma(x, m, s), a, Inf)$value / k
    return(c(m1, m2 - m1^2))
  }
  if (dist == "beta") return(c(m / (m + s), m * s / ((m + s)^2 * (m + s + 1))))
  al <- (a - m) / s; be <- (b - m) / s
  Z <- pnorm(be) - pnorm(al)
  dal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), dnorm(al), 0); dbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), dnorm(be), 0)
  aal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), al * dnorm(al), 0); bbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), be * dnorm(be), 0)
  c(m + s * (dal - dbe) / Z, s^2 * (1 + (aal - bbe) / Z - ((dal - dbe) / Z)^2))
}
pmom <- prior_spec |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pm = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper, dist)[1], pv = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper, dist)[2]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(variable, pm, pv)
contraction <- conv |>
  inner_join(pmom, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(contraction = 1 - sd^2 / pv, z = (mean - pm) / sd, fit = fit_lab[fit],
         lab = pm_lab[variable])
contraction |>
  ggplot(aes(contraction, z, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab), parse = TRUE, size = 2.8, seed = 1,
                           show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(NA, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Posterior contraction", y = "Posterior z-score")
```

```{r}
low_c <- contraction |> filter(fit == fit_lab[["first"]], contraction < 0.5)
hi_z <- contraction |> filter(abs(z) > 2)
final_ok <- contraction$variable[contraction$fit == fit_lab[["final"]] & contraction$contraction >= 0.5]
low_final <- setdiff(unique(contraction$variable), final_ok)
low_final_text <- if (length(low_final) == 0) {
  "By the end of the season every parameter contracts by more than half."
} else {
  paste0("By the end of the season every parameter except ", sym_list(low_final), " contracts by more than half.")
}
hi_z_text <- if (nrow(hi_z) == 0) {
  "No posterior lies more than two of its own standard deviations from its prior mean."
} else {
  paste0("Posteriors more than two of their own standard deviations from the prior mean are ",
         paste0("$", sym_lab[hi_z$variable], "$ (", tolower(sub(".*, ", "", hi_z$fit)),
                ", $z = ", fmt(hi_z$z, 1), "$)", collapse = "; "),
         ". These sit in the tail of their priors: not a failure of fit, but a sign that for that fit the prior is tighter than the data would choose. @sec-supp-perturb checks whether it matters for the published ratings.")
}
```

In week 1, `r nrow(low_c)` of `r n_distinct(contraction$variable)` structural parameters contract by less than half --- `r sym_list(low_c$variable)` --- so their priors carry the fit, as intended in a week with one game per team. `r low_final_text` `r hi_z_text`

## Justification of the Informative Priors {#sec-supp-justify}

Informative priors need a justification that does not come from the data they are applied to. Ours come from the history of the sport. The structural parameters describe the game rather than any team --- how much a home field is worth, how noisy a margin is, how far FCS teams sit below FBS teams, how much of a team's strength carries over a summer --- and they should change little from year to year. The `prior_refits` target checks this directly: it refits the full-season posterior of every complete season, each with about 1,550 games, under deliberately vague priors --- $\eta \sim \mathcal N(0, 10^2)$, tier offsets $\mathcal N(0, 100^2)$, $\beta$ nearly uniform on $(0, 1)$, half-normal priors with scale 25 on $\tau_\ell$ and $\omega$, scale 2 on $\lambda$ and $\kappa$, and scale 50 on $\sigma_e$ and $\sigma_m$, and comparably wide priors on the total model and the family's shape parameters --- so that a season's estimate owes nothing to the published priors. The random-walk steps get wide priors centred away from zero, $\mathcal N^+(0.8, 0.8^2)$ for $\phi_r$ and $\mathcal N^+(1, 0.8^2)$ for $\phi_t$, because under one with its mode at zero the sampler stalls in the funnel at small $\phi_r$ (@sec-hierarchy); $\nu$ gets $\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 0.05)$, with mean 40, and the preseason coefficients normal priors several times wider than their estimates. @fig-supp-justify plots the resulting per-season posteriors against the priors now in use, and @tbl-supp-justify gives the numbers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-justify
#| fig-cap: "Per-season full-season posteriors under vague priors (points: mean; bars: $\\pm 2$ posterior sd) against the prior now in use (line: prior mean; bands: $\\pm 1$ and $\\pm 2$ prior sd). The priors are centred on the recency-weighted mean of the seasons after the first, with the predictive standard deviation of @eq-pool."
#| fig-scap: "Per-season posteriors against the priors"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
pri_band <- pri |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab))
struct |>
  filter(variable %in% pri$variable) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, mean)) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_hline(data = pri_band, aes(yintercept = mean), colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd), colour = col_ref, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1, colour = col_ink) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2015, 2020, 2025)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-justify
#| tbl-cap: "Empirical basis of the structural priors: the pooled mean of the per-season full-season posterior means under vague priors, their between-season standard deviation, the typical within-season posterior sd (root mean square), and the prior now in use. \\emph{Ratio} is the prior sd over the between-season sd; \\emph{LOSO} is the share of seasons whose own estimate lies within two standard deviations of the prior pooled from the other seasons, counting the estimate's own posterior sd."
# Leave-one-season-out: is each season's estimate inside the prior pooled from the others?
loso_z <- targets::tar_read(prior_loso_check, store = store)
loso_cov <- loso_z |> group_by(variable) |> summarise(cov = mean(abs(z) <= 2)) |> (\(d) setNames(d$cov, d$variable))()
pooled |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  inner_join(pri, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab))) |>
  arrange(variable) |>
  transmute(Parameter = tex_lab[as.character(variable)], `Pooled mean` = fmt(pooled_mean, 2),
            `Between-season sd` = fmt(between_sd, 2), `Posterior sd` = fmt(typical_post_sd, 2),
            `Prior mean` = fmt(mean, 2), `Prior sd` = fmt(sd, 2), Ratio = fmt(sd / between_sd, 1),
            LOSO = pct(loso_cov[as.character(variable)])) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrrrr")
```

Four points qualify this justification. First, pooling every complete season is empirical Bayes at the level of the sport, and saying that a season's estimate lies inside a prior partly built from it would be circular. The last column of @tbl-supp-justify avoids that: for each season it pools the *other* seasons only and asks whether the season's own estimate lies within two standard deviations of that leave-one-season-out prior, where the standard deviation combines the prior's with the estimate's own posterior standard deviation. For every parameter it does in `r pct(min(loso_cov[pri$variable], na.rm = TRUE))` or more of seasons, so a new season should be expected to fall inside its prior. Second, `r first_season` is left out of the pooling for the structural reason given in @sec-priors, and 2020 for $\eta$. Third, the prior standard deviation removes estimation noise from the between-season spread (@eq-pool). For `r sym_list(noise_pars)` that spread is about the size of the within-season posterior sd, so their priors are narrow, as narrow as the uncertainty of a mean over about `r fmt(median(pooled$n_eff), 0)` effective seasons. That is the right width if the parameter is the same every season, and the leave-one-season-out column checks it. Fourth, the priors in use are copied into the configuration from one run of the refits and lag them by a rebuild: `r { dz <- pooled |> inner_join(pri, by = "variable") |> mutate(z = abs(pooled_mean - mean) / sd); paste0(sum(dz$z > 0.5), " of the ", nrow(dz), " prior means ", if (sum(dz$z > 0.5) == 1) "is" else "are", " more than half a prior sd from the current pooled mean", if (any(dz$z > 0.5)) paste0(" (", sym_list(dz$variable[dz$z > 0.5]), ")") else "") }`.

## Induced Priors {#sec-supp-induced}

A prior on parameters induces a prior on everything computed from them, and a set of individually reasonable priors can combine into an unreasonable one. The quantities that matter here are not $\omega$ or $\tau_1$ but the spread of team strengths, the probability that the home team wins an even game, and the distribution of margins the model expects before seeing any game. @tbl-supp-induced simulates them from the priors alone, with the `r last_full` schedule and carry-over, each game played at the random-walk states of its week and its margin drawn from the `r fam_name[[fam]]` law, and @fig-supp-induced compares the prior predictive distribution of three margin statistics with the values observed that season.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-induced
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Induced priors, by simulation from the priors alone (4,000 draws) on the ", last_full, " schedule, with the carry-over $d_i$ from ", last_full - 1, ". The last column gives the value observed in ", last_full, " where one exists.")'
ip <- targets::tar_read(induced_prior, store = store)
ind_lab <- c(
  sigma_marg = "Marginal margin scale $\\bar\\sigma$ (pts)",
  r2 = "Share of margin variance from efficiency, $R^2$",
  nu = "Degrees of freedom $\\nu$",
  tau = "Weekly random-walk step $\\phi_r$ (pts)",
  sd_fbs = "SD of FBS strengths (pts)",
  top_minus_12 = "Best minus 12th-best FBS team (pts)",
  p_home_even = "P(home win), evenly matched teams",
  p_top_vs_avg = "P(best FBS team beats an average one), neutral",
  sd_margin = "SD of regulation margin, all games (pts)",
  within7 = "Share of games within 7 points",
  home_win = "Home win rate, true home games"
)
if (!has_nu) ind_lab <- ind_lab[names(ind_lab) != "nu"]
ip$draws |>
  select(all_of(names(ind_lab))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), q50 = median(value), q95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(obs = ip$observed[name], name = factor(name, levels = names(ind_lab))) |>
  arrange(name) |>
  transmute(Quantity = ind_lab[as.character(name)], `5\\%` = fmt(q05, 2), Median = fmt(q50, 2),
            `95\\%` = fmt(q95, 2), Observed = ifelse(is.na(obs), "", fmt(obs, 2))) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-induced
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Prior predictive distributions of three statistics of the ", last_full, " regulation margins, simulated from the priors alone; the vertical line is the observed value.", if (any(ip$draws$sd_margin > 60)) paste0(" The SD panel omits the ", pct(mean(ip$draws$sd_margin > 60), 1), " of draws above 60 points (see text).") else "")'
#| fig-scap: "Prior predictive checks"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.32
ip_lab <- c(sd_margin = "SD of margin", within7 = "Share within 7 pts", home_win = "Home win rate")
ip$draws |>
  select(all_of(names(ip_lab))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  filter(!(name == "sd_margin" & value > 60)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(ip_lab[name], levels = ip_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = col_ref, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(name = factor(ip_lab, levels = ip_lab), obs = ip$observed[names(ip_lab)]),
             aes(xintercept = obs), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Prior draws")
```

```{r}
ipq <- function(v, p) quantile(ip$draws[[v]], p, names = FALSE)
ip_in <- map_lgl(names(ip_lab), \(v) ip$observed[[v]] >= ipq(v, 0.025) & ip$observed[[v]] <= ipq(v, 0.975))
```

The induced priors are on the scale of the sport: before any game, the model expects the best FBS team to be about `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.5), 0)` points better than the twelfth (90\% prior interval `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.05), 0)`--`r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.95), 0)`), an even game to be won at home `r pct(ipq("p_home_even", 0.5))` of the time, and margins with a standard deviation of about `r fmt(ipq("sd_margin", 0.5), 0)` points. `r sum(ip_in)` of the three observed statistics lie inside the central 95\% of their prior predictive distribution`r if (!all(ip_in)) paste0("; the exception is the ", paste(tolower(ip_lab[!ip_in]), collapse = " and "), ", the statistic the fitted model also misses (@sec-ppc)") else ""`. Three induced quantities deserve care. The first is the tail of the margin law. A vague prior on $\nu$ such as $\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$ puts `r pct(pgamma(3, 2, 0.1), 1)` of its mass below 3, where the $t$ law has little or no variance, and such draws produce prior-predictive seasons with a margin standard deviation of 50 points or more: an implausible implication of a prior on one parameter for an observable. The pooled prior avoids it, because every season's vague-prior estimate of $\nu$ lies between `r fmt(min(struct$mean[struct$variable == "nu"]), 0)` and `r fmt(max(struct$mean[struct$variable == "nu"]), 0)` (@tbl-priors-other): `r pct(mean(ip$draws$nu < 3), 1)` of its draws fall below 3, and the 99th percentile of the prior-predictive margin standard deviation is `r fmt(ipq("sd_margin", 0.99), 0)` points. The spread of FBS strengths combines $\omega$, $\tau_1$ and $\beta d_i$, so a prior that looks modest for each piece can imply a wide or narrow league; the table shows it lands at a plausible `r fmt(ipq("sd_fbs", 0.5), 0)` points. And the prior on $\bar\sigma = (\sigma_m^2 + \kappa^2\sigma_e^2)^{1/2}$, which with the family's shape parameters sets every win probability and therefore every $\pi_g$ in the resume, is induced by three separate priors; its 90\% prior interval, `r fmt(ipq("sigma_marg", 0.05), 1)`--`r fmt(ipq("sigma_marg", 0.95), 1)` points, is narrow, which is appropriate only because each of the three is well estimated in every season (@fig-supp-justify).

## Posterior Predictive Checks {#sec-supp-ppc}

@sec-ppc compared four summary statistics with their replicates. Here the whole distributions are compared (@fig-supp-dens), and then the location and spread of the margin within each kind of matchup (@fig-supp-stat-grouped), since a model that fits the pooled distribution can still misfit a subgroup, in particular the games across tiers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-dens
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Observed distribution (black) against 50 replicated data sets (orange) for the ", fit_lab[["final"]], " fit. Left: regulation margin, home minus away, replicated from the marginal law of @eq-lik-marg and rounded. Right: efficiency margin, for games that have one.")'
#| fig-scap: "Posterior predictive densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
fin <- sup$final
he <- fin$played$has_eff
rep_long <- bind_rows(
  as_tibble(t(fin$yrep[1:50, ]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Regulation margin"),
  as_tibble(t(fin$erep[1:50, he]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Efficiency margin")
)
obs_long <- bind_rows(tibble(value = fin$played$margin, signal = "Regulation margin"),
                      tibble(value = fin$played$eff[he], signal = "Efficiency margin"))
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = rep_long, aes(value, group = rep), colour = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.2, bw = 3) +
  geom_density(data = obs_long, aes(value), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7, bw = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin", "Efficiency margin")), scales = "free") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-80, 80)) +
  labs(x = "Points, home minus away", y = "Density")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-stat-grouped
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Grouped test statistics, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". Histograms: the mean and standard deviation of the regulation margin over 400 replicated data sets (as in @fig-ppc), within each kind of matchup; vertical line: the observed value. The label gives the posterior predictive $p$-value, the share of replicates at least as large as the observed statistic.")'
#| fig-scap: "Grouped posterior predictive test statistics"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
tier_name <- c("FBS", "FCS", "Lower")
grp <- with(fin, {
  th <- teams$tier[played$home]; ta <- teams$tier[played$away]
  paste(tier_name[pmin(th, ta)], tier_name[pmax(th, ta)], sep = "--")
})
grp_keep <- names(which(table(grp) >= 30))
stat_rep <- map_dfr(grp_keep, function(gname) {
  idx <- grp == gname
  bind_rows(
    tibble(stat = "Mean", value = rowMeans(fin$yrep[, idx, drop = FALSE])),
    tibble(stat = "SD", value = apply(fin$yrep[, idx, drop = FALSE], 1, sd))
  ) |> mutate(group = paste0(gname, " (", sum(idx), ")"),
              obs = ifelse(stat == "Mean", mean(fin$played$margin[idx]), sd(fin$played$margin[idx])))
})
stat_p <- stat_rep |> group_by(group, stat) |>
  summarise(obs = first(obs), p = mean(value >= obs), .groups = "drop")
stat_rep |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = col_ref, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = stat_p, aes(xintercept = obs), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = stat_p, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste0("p = ", fmt(p, 2))),
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.4, size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(stat ~ group, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Replicates")
```

```{r}
stat_out <- stat_p |> filter(p < 0.025 | p > 0.975)
stat_out_text <- if (nrow(stat_out) == 0) {
  "none falls outside $(0.025, 0.975)$"
} else {
  paste0(nrow(stat_out), if (nrow(stat_out) == 1) " falls" else " fall", " outside $(0.025, 0.975)$: the ",
         paste(tolower(stat_out$stat), "in", sub(" [(].*", "", stat_out$group), "games", collapse = " and the "),
         ", where the observed value is ", ifelse(stat_out$p > 0.975, "smaller", "larger"),
         " than almost every replicate")
}
```

Across the `r nrow(stat_p)` grouped statistics the posterior predictive $p$-values run from `r fmt(min(stat_p$p), 2)` to `r fmt(max(stat_p$p), 2)`, and `r stat_out_text`. The tier offsets therefore place cross-tier games about right in location, and the misfit of @sec-ppc is mainly one of shape. Games across tiers are, if anything, less variable than a single margin scale for all games allows: a tier-specific scale is a natural refinement. The density overlay shows the same shape misfit directly: the observed margin has a sharper peak near zero than any replicate.

The leave-one-out probability integral transform (LOO-PIT) checks calibration game by game without using a game to predict itself: for each game, $\Pr(y_g^{\text{rep}} \le y_g \mid \text{all other games})$, estimated with the Pareto-smoothed importance weights of the LOO computation. If the model is calibrated these values are uniform; a U shape indicates predictive distributions that are too narrow, a hump that they are too wide [@gabryVisualizationBayesianWorkflow2019; @sailynojaGraphicalTestDiscrete2022]. @fig-supp-pit shows them for both signals and both fits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pit
#| fig-cap: "LOO-PIT histograms, 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. Margins are whole numbers while the model is continuous, which spreads each PIT value over an interval of width about $1/\\bar\\sigma \\approx 0.08$ and does not by itself cause non-uniformity at this bin width."
#| fig-scap: "LOO-PIT histograms"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.6
pit_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  bind_rows(tibble(pit = fit$pit_margin, signal = "Regulation margin"),
            tibble(pit = fit$pit_eff, signal = "Efficiency margin")) |>
    filter(!is.na(pit)) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin", "Efficiency margin")))
pit_band <- pit_df |> count(fit, signal) |>
  mutate(lo = qbinom(0.025, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20), hi = qbinom(0.975, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20))
pit_df |>
  ggplot(aes(pit)) +
  geom_rect(data = pit_band, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05),
                 fill = col_power, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(signal ~ fit) +
  labs(x = "LOO-PIT", y = "Density")
```

```{r}
pit_out <- pit_df |>
  mutate(bin = pmin(floor(pit * 20) + 1, 20)) |>
  count(fit, signal, bin) |>
  left_join(pit_df |> count(fit, signal, name = "N"), by = c("fit", "signal")) |>
  mutate(out = n < qbinom(0.025, N, 0.05) | n > qbinom(0.975, N, 0.05)) |>
  summarise(out = sum(out), bins = n())
```

Of the `r pit_out$bins` histogram bins across the four panels, `r pit_out$out` fall outside their 95\% band, against about `r fmt(0.05 * pit_out$bins, 0)` expected by chance. There is no U shape or hump, so the predictive distributions are neither systematically too narrow nor too wide, in week 1 or at the end of the season.

@fig-supp-resid plots the observed margin minus its posterior mean against that mean. A systematic trend would mean that the model's spreads are biased for lopsided or for close matchups --- for example, if strong favourites won by less than predicted.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-resid
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Residual regulation margin against the posterior mean margin, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". The line is a LOESS smooth with a 95\\% band; points are games, by kind of matchup.")'
#| fig-scap: "Residuals against predicted margin"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.5
tibble(mu = fin$mu_mean, resid = fin$played$margin - fin$mu_mean,
       group = ifelse(grp == "FBS--FBS", "FBS--FBS", "Other")) |>
  ggplot(aes(mu, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = col_power, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FBS--FBS` = col_ink, Other = col_ref)) +
  labs(x = "Posterior mean margin (points)", y = "Observed minus mean (points)")
```

## Influence and PSIS Diagnostics {#sec-supp-loo}

The Pareto $\hat k$ of each game estimates the tail shape of its importance ratios in PSIS-LOO; values above 0.7 mean the leave-one-out approximation is unreliable for that game, and in practice that the game is highly influential on the posterior [@vehtariParetoSmoothedImportance2024]. @fig-supp-khat plots every game's $\hat k$ in both fits, and @tbl-supp-khat lists the games above 0.7 in the final fit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-khat
#| fig-cap: "Pareto $\\hat k$ for each game, in schedule order. Dashed lines at 0.5 and 0.7."
#| fig-scap: "Pareto k diagnostics"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  tibble(game = seq_along(fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k), k = fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k,
         cross = fit$teams$tier[fit$played$home] != fit$teams$tier[fit$played$away],
         fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  ggplot(aes(game, k)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 0.7), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = cross), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_ref, `TRUE` = col_ink),
                      labels = c(`FALSE` = "Same tier", `TRUE` = "Across tiers")) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Game", y = expression(hat(k)))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-khat
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Games with Pareto $\\hat k > 0.7$ in the ", fit_lab[["final"]], " fit, largest first. \\emph{Games} counts each team''s games in the fit.")'
gp <- table(factor(c(fin$played$home, fin$played$away), levels = seq_len(nrow(fin$teams))))
esc <- \(x) gsub("&", "\\&", x, fixed = TRUE)
khat_tab <- tibble(k = fin$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k, h = fin$played$home, a = fin$played$away,
                   hp = fin$played$home_points, ap = fin$played$away_points, wk = fin$played$week_seq) |>
  filter(k > 0.7) |>
  arrange(desc(k))
if (nrow(khat_tab) > 0) {
  khat_tab |>
    transmute(Week = wk,
              Home = sprintf("%s (%s, %d)", esc(fin$teams$team[h]), tier_name[fin$teams$tier[h]], gp[h]),
              Away = sprintf("%s (%s, %d)", esc(fin$teams$team[a]), tier_name[fin$teams$tier[a]], gp[a]),
              Score = paste0(hp, "--", ap), `$\\hat k$` = fmt(k, 2)) |>
    rename(`Home (tier, games)` = Home, `Away (tier, games)` = Away) |>
    ktab(align = "rllrr")
}
```

```{r}
k_first <- sum(sup$first$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7)
k_final <- nrow(khat_tab)
k_lower <- sum(fin$teams$tier[khat_tab$h] == 3L | fin$teams$tier[khat_tab$a] == 3L)
k_fbs <- sum(fin$teams$tier[khat_tab$h] == 1L | fin$teams$tier[khat_tab$a] == 1L)
k_single <- sum(pmin(gp[khat_tab$h], gp[khat_tab$a]) == 1L)
```

`r k_final` of `r fmt(nrow(fin$played))` games exceed 0.7 in the final fit and `r k_first` of `r fmt(nrow(sup$first$played))` in week 1. In the final fit `r k_lower` of them involve a lower-division team and `r k_single` are the only game of one of the two teams: such a game is the only evidence about that team, so removing it changes the team's posterior completely. `r if (k_fbs == 0) "None involves an FBS team" else paste0(k_fbs, " involve an FBS team")`, and the estimated expected log predictive density is not materially affected. A $K$-fold refit would remove the approximation for these games if it were needed.

## Power-scaling Sensitivity {#sec-supp-powerscale}

@tbl-sens summarised power-scaling sensitivity by a single distance per parameter. @fig-supp-powerscale shows what lies behind it for the parameters flagged most often: the posterior density as the prior (top row) or the likelihood (bottom row) is raised to powers between 0.8 and 1.25 [@kallioinenDetectingDiagnosingPrior2024]. A density that shifts with the prior power is prior-sensitive; one that shifts with the likelihood power is informed by the data.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-powerscale
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Power-scaled posterior densities, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". Darker lines are larger powers $\\alpha$; the base posterior is $\\alpha = 1$.")'
#| fig-scap: "Power-scaled posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
ps <- fin$powerscale
flag_vars <- flag_counts |> filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  arrange(desc(conflict + weak)) |> slice_head(n = 5) |> pull(variable)
if (!is.null(ps)) {
  get_side <- function(side_list, side) {
    map_dfr(side_list, function(d) {
      a <- attr(d, "powerscaling")$alpha
      posterior::as_draws_df(d) |> as_tibble() |>
        select(any_of(flag_vars), any_of(".log_weight")) |>
        mutate(alpha = a)
    }) |> mutate(side = side)
  }
  base <- posterior::as_draws_df(ps$base_draws) |> as_tibble() |> select(any_of(flag_vars)) |>
    mutate(alpha = 1)
  sides <- bind_rows(
    get_side(c(ps$prior_scaled$draws_sequence), "Prior scaled"),
    get_side(c(ps$likelihood_scaled$draws_sequence), "Likelihood scaled")
  )
  sides <- bind_rows(sides, mutate(base, side = "Prior scaled"), mutate(base, side = "Likelihood scaled"))
  if (!".log_weight" %in% names(sides)) sides$.log_weight <- 0
  sides |>
    mutate(.log_weight = coalesce(.log_weight, 0)) |>
    group_by(side, alpha) |>
    mutate(w = exp(.log_weight - max(.log_weight)), w = w / sum(w)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    pivot_longer(any_of(flag_vars), names_to = "variable") |>
    mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab),
           side = factor(side, levels = c("Prior scaled", "Likelihood scaled"),
                         labels = c("Prior~scaled", "Likelihood~scaled"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, weight = w, group = alpha, colour = alpha)) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 0.35, adjust = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "gray80", high = col_power, name = expression(alpha)) +
    facet_wrap(side ~ variable, scales = "free", nrow = 2, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text())
}
```

## Sensitivity to the Prior: Perturbation Refits {#sec-supp-perturb}

Power-scaling is a local check: it asks what happens under small multiplicative changes to the prior. The requirement that matters in practice is global --- that a reasonable analyst with a different prior would publish essentially the same ratings. We therefore refit both posteriors under four joint alternatives for every structural prior: all prior standard deviations doubled, all multiplied by five (close to vague on the scale of these parameters), and all prior means moved up, or down, by one prior standard deviation. The last two move every mean at once in the same direction, a deliberately harsh test. The family's shape parameters ($\nu$ and $\gamma$) are pooled like the others and move with them; the mean and standard deviation of the Gamma prior on $\nu$ are moved and matched back to a Gamma. Joint changes can cancel, so each prior group is also widened fivefold on its own. @tbl-supp-perturb-par gives the structural posteriors and @tbl-supp-perturb-out compares what is published: the FBS power ratings and the resume. @tbl-supp-perturb-single gives the one-at-a-time results, and @tbl-supp-perturb-2020 repeats the joint alternatives for 2020, the most atypical season.

```{r}
ps_all <- targets::tar_read(prior_sensitivity, store = store)
sc_joint <- c("Baseline", "SD x 2", "SD x 5", "Means + 1 SD", "Means - 1 SD")
grp_tex <- c(hfa = "$\\eta$", tier = "$m_2, m_3$", b_prev = "$\\beta$", sigma_team = "$\\tau_\\ell$",
             sigma_conf = "$\\omega$", lambda = "$\\lambda$", kappa = "$\\kappa$", sigma_eff = "$\\sigma_e$",
             sigma_m = "$\\sigma_m$", tau = "$\\phi_r, \\phi_t$", family = if (fam == "scale_t") "$\\nu, \\gamma$" else "$\\nu$",
             total = "total-model", preseason = "preseason terms")
grp_tex <- grp_tex[names(grp_tex) %in% unique(sub("SD x 5: ", "", map_chr(ps_all, "scenario")))]
sc_single <- paste0("SD x 5: ", names(grp_tex))
sc_levels <- c(sc_joint, sc_single)
sc_tex <- c(Baseline = "Baseline", `SD x 2` = "SD $\\times$ 2", `SD x 5` = "SD $\\times$ 5",
            `Means + 1 SD` = "Means $+$1 SD", `Means - 1 SD` = "Means $-$1 SD",
            setNames(paste0(grp_tex, " sd $\\times$ 5"), sc_single))
ps_par <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$par, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
ps_rat <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$ratings, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
ps_health <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$health, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-par
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior means (posterior sd) of selected structural parameters under each prior. \\emph{Gates} reports whether the refit passed the convergence gates of @sec-gates."
show_vars <- c("hfa", "b_prev", "sigma_m", "kappa", "sigma_conf", "mu_tier[2]")
ps_par |>
  filter(variable %in% show_vars, scenario %in% sc_joint) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%s {\\scriptsize(%s)}", fmt(mean, 2), fmt(sd, 2)),
         variable = factor(variable, levels = show_vars)) |>
  select(fit, scenario, variable, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = cell) |>
  left_join(ps_health |> select(fit, scenario, passed), by = c("fit", "scenario")) |>
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)) |>
  arrange(fit, scenario) |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "Baseline", sub(paste0(last_full, ", "), "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""),
         Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)], Gates = ifelse(passed, "pass", "fail")) |>
  select(Fit, Prior, all_of(show_vars), Gates) |>
  rename_with(\(v) paste0("$", sym_lab[v], "$"), all_of(show_vars)) |>
  ktab(align = paste0("ll", strrep("r", length(show_vars)), "l"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-out
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of the prior on the published FBS products, relative to the baseline prior. Power: Spearman correlation of the ratings, and the mean and largest absolute change in a team's rating (points). Resume: Spearman correlation of $\\WAB$, the largest change in resume rank among the baseline top 25, and the number of teams whose membership of the top 12 changes."
perturb_summary <- function(rat) {
  base <- rat |> filter(scenario == "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
    select(fit, team_id, power0 = power, wab0 = wab, rr0 = resume_rank)
  rat |>
    filter(scenario != "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
    inner_join(base, by = c("fit", "team_id")) |>
    group_by(fit, scenario) |>
    summarise(
      rho_power = cor(power, power0, method = "spearman"),
      mad_power = mean(abs(power - power0)), max_power = max(abs(power - power0)),
      rho_wab = cor(wab, wab0, method = "spearman"),
      max_rank = max(abs(resume_rank - rr0)[rr0 <= 25]),
      top12 = sum(xor(resume_rank <= 12, rr0 <= 12)) / 2,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)) |>
    arrange(fit, scenario)
}
perturb_tab <- function(po, first_scenario) {
  po |>
    mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == first_scenario, sub("^[0-9]+, ", "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""),
           Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)]) |>
    transmute(Fit, Prior, `$\\rho$ power` = fmt(rho_power, 3), `Mean $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(mad_power, 2),
              `Max $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(max_power, 2), `$\\rho$ WAB` = fmt(rho_wab, 3),
              `Max rank $\\Delta$ (top 25)` = max_rank, `Top-12 changes` = fmt(top12, 0)) |>
    ktab(align = "llrrrrrr")
}
base <- ps_rat |> filter(scenario == "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
  select(fit, team_id, power0 = power, wab0 = wab, rr0 = resume_rank)
perturb_all <- perturb_summary(ps_rat)
perturb_out <- perturb_all |> filter(scenario %in% sc_joint)
perturb_single <- perturb_all |> filter(scenario %in% sc_single)
perturb_out |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "SD x 2", sub(paste0(last_full, ", "), "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""),
         Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)]) |>
  transmute(Fit, Prior, `$\\rho$ power` = fmt(rho_power, 3), `Mean $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(mad_power, 2),
            `Max $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(max_power, 2), `$\\rho$ WAB` = fmt(rho_wab, 3),
            `Max rank $\\Delta$ (top 25)` = max_rank, `Top-12 changes` = fmt(top12, 0)) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-perturb
#| fig-cap: "Change in each FBS team's power rating relative to the baseline prior, by alternative prior. Each point is a team; the box spans the middle half. The week-1 ratings depend on the prior by design, the final ratings hardly at all."
#| fig-scap: "Change in power ratings under alternative priors"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
ps_rat |>
  filter(scenario %in% setdiff(sc_joint, "Baseline"), tier == 1) |>
  inner_join(base, by = c("fit", "team_id")) |>
  mutate(delta = power - power0, scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_joint),
         fit = factor(fit_lab[fit], levels = fit_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(scenario, delta)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4, colour = col_ref) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, colour = col_power, width = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~fit) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change in power rating (points)")
```

```{r}
pf <- perturb_out |> filter(fit == "final")
p1 <- perturb_out |> filter(fit == "first")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-single
#| tbl-cap: "One prior group at a time: each group's prior standard deviation multiplied by five, all others at baseline. Columns as in @tbl-supp-perturb-out."
perturb_tab(perturb_single, sc_single[1])
ps_single_max <- perturb_single |> group_by(fit) |> slice_max(max_power, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-2020
#| tbl-cap: "The joint prior alternatives for the 2020 season (week 1 and the final posterior). Columns as in @tbl-supp-perturb-out."
ps2020_rat <- map_dfr(ps2020, \(x) mutate(x$ratings, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
perturb_2020 <- perturb_summary(ps2020_rat)
fit_lab_2020 <- c(first = "2020, week 1", final = "2020, final")
perturb_2020 |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "SD x 2", fit_lab_2020[as.character(fit)], ""), Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)]) |>
  transmute(Fit, Prior, `$\\rho$ power` = fmt(rho_power, 3), `Mean $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(mad_power, 2),
            `Max $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(max_power, 2), `$\\rho$ WAB` = fmt(rho_wab, 3),
            `Max rank $\\Delta$ (top 25)` = max_rank, `Top-12 changes` = fmt(top12, 0)) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrr")
p20 <- perturb_2020 |> filter(fit == "final")
```

At the end of the season the prior is immaterial to what is published: under every alternative the FBS power ratings correlate with the baseline at $\rho `r if (min(pf$rho_power) >= 0.9995) "> 0.999" else paste("\\ge", fmt(min(pf$rho_power), 3))`$, no team's rating moves by more than `r fmt(max(pf$max_power), 1)` points (mean `r fmt(max(pf$mad_power), 2)`), and `r if (max(pf$top12) == 0) "the resume top 12 is unchanged" else paste0("at most ", fmt(max(pf$top12), 0), " team(s) enter or leave the resume top 12")`. More strikingly, the week-1 ratings are also robust, although several structural posteriors there stay close to their priors (@sec-supp-prior): widening every prior fivefold moves no FBS rating by more than `r fmt(p1$max_power[p1$scenario == "SD x 5"], 1)` points, shifting every prior mean by one prior standard deviation moves none by more than `r fmt(max(p1$max_power[grepl("Means", p1$scenario)]), 1)`, and the ratings keep their order ($\rho \ge `r fmt(min(p1$rho_power), 3)`$). The reason is that a week-1 rating rests mainly on the carry-over $\beta d_i$ from last season's final ratings, and $\beta$ is estimated from the week-1 games together with last season's ratings, whatever its prior; the priors on the scales and offsets change how much each team is shrunk towards its conference, which moves ratings by a point or two, not their order. The structural priors therefore stabilise the sampler in data-poor weeks (@sec-priors) without determining what is published. The priors on lower-division offsets and spreads, which the diagnostics flag most, affect FBS ratings only through the handful of cross-tier games.

One prior group at a time (@tbl-supp-perturb-single), the largest effect in the final fit comes from widening the prior on `r grp_tex[sub("SD x 5: ", "", as.character(ps_single_max$scenario[ps_single_max$fit == "final"]))]`, which moves no FBS rating by more than `r fmt(ps_single_max$max_power[ps_single_max$fit == "final"], 1)` points; in week 1 it is the prior on `r grp_tex[sub("SD x 5: ", "", as.character(ps_single_max$scenario[ps_single_max$fit == "first"]))]`, at `r fmt(ps_single_max$max_power[ps_single_max$fit == "first"], 1)` points. For 2020 (@tbl-supp-perturb-2020), a season with atypical home field, few early games and a spring FCS season, the final ratings under the joint alternatives keep a rank correlation of at least `r fmt(min(p20$rho_power), 3)` and no rating moved by more than `r fmt(max(p20$max_power), 1)` points.

## Simulation-based Calibration {#sec-supp-sbc}

The checks so far ask whether the model fits the data. Simulation-based calibration asks whether the *computation* recovers the model: if parameters are drawn from the prior, data simulated from them, and the posterior computed, then the rank of each true value among the posterior draws is uniform when the sampler and the code are correct [@taltsValidatingBayesianInference2018; @modrakSimulationBasedCalibration2023]. We simulate `r n_distinct(sbc$ranks$sim)` seasons on the real `r sbc$season` schedule through week `r sbc$week` (`r fmt(sbc$n_games)` games, with the same pattern of missing efficiency margins and the same carry-over $d_i$ and $s_i$), each with its own random walk and margins from the `r fam_name[[fam]]` law, refit each with four chains of 250 draws, and rank the true values among `r sbc$n_rank_draws` thinned draws. The simulation covers the margin model only; the total model, which shares no parameter with it, is switched off. Besides structural parameters the test quantities include what is published: every FBS team's centred power rating, its $\WAB$ (the true value computed from the true strengths and the simulated results), and both ranks.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-sbc
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Simulation-based calibration, ", n_distinct(sbc$ranks$sim), " simulated seasons. Histograms of the rank of the true value among ", sbc$n_rank_draws, " posterior draws, in 10 bins; the band is the central 99\\% range of a bin count under uniformity (for the team-level quantities, pooled over all FBS teams, so the band is narrow). The label gives the coverage of the central 80\\% posterior interval.")'
#| fig-scap: "Simulation-based calibration"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
sbc_r <- sbc$ranks |> mutate(bin = pmin(floor(rank / ((sbc$n_rank_draws + 1) / 10)), 9))
sbc_lab <- c(hfa = "eta", b_prev = "beta", sigma_m = "sigma[m]", lambda = "lambda", kappa = "kappa",
             sigma_conf = "omega", nu = "nu", gamma_m = "gamma", p_wide = "p[w]", sigma_w = "sigma[w]",
             tau_r = "phi[r]", b_ret = "beta[q]", c_ret = "gamma[q]", b_tal = "gamma[a]", b_prev2 = "beta[2]",
             b_prev_low = "beta[low]", delta_coach = "delta[c]", `Power rating` = "Power~rating", WAB = "WAB",
             `Power rank` = "Power~rank", `Resume rank` = "Resume~rank")
sbc_lab <- sbc_lab[names(sbc_lab) %in% unique(sbc$ranks$quantity)]
sbc_cnt <- sbc_r |> count(quantity, bin) |> group_by(quantity) |> mutate(N = sum(n)) |> ungroup()
sbc_band <- sbc_cnt |> distinct(quantity, N) |> mutate(lo = qbinom(0.005, N, 0.1), hi = qbinom(0.995, N, 0.1))
sbc_cov <- sbc_r |> group_by(quantity) |> summarise(cov = mean(covered), .groups = "drop")
sbc_chi <- sbc_cnt |> group_by(quantity) |>
  summarise(p = pchisq(sum((n - N / 10)^2 / (N / 10)), df = 9, lower.tail = FALSE), .groups = "drop")
fac <- function(q) factor(q, levels = names(sbc_lab), labels = sbc_lab)
ggplot(sbc_cnt |> mutate(q = fac(quantity))) +
  geom_rect(data = sbc_band |> mutate(q = fac(quantity)), aes(xmin = -0.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
            fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_col(aes(bin, n), fill = col_power, alpha = 0.85, width = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = sbc_cov |> mutate(q = fac(quantity)), aes(x = 4.5, y = Inf, label = paste0("80%: ", round(100 * cov))),
            vjust = 1.3, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~q, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Rank of the true value (10 bins)", y = "Count")
team_q <- c("Power rating", "WAB", "Power rank", "Resume rank")
```

The structural parameters are recovered with coverage of the 80\% interval between `r pct(min(sbc_cov$cov[!sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]))` and `r pct(max(sbc_cov$cov[!sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]))`, and for the published quantities it is `r paste0(tolower(sbc_cov$quantity[sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]), " ", pct(sbc_cov$cov[sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]), collapse = ", ")`. `r { bad <- sbc_chi |> filter(p < 0.01); if (nrow(bad)) paste0("A chi-square test of uniformity of the rank histograms rejects at the 1% level for ", paste(bad$quantity, collapse = ", "), "; with ", fmt(sum(!is.na(sbc$ranks$team)) / n_distinct(sbc$ranks$sim)), " team-level values per simulated season the team-level tests are very sensitive, and the rank statistics of different teams in one simulation are not independent, so the size of the departure, visible in the figure, matters more than its significance.") else "A chi-square test of uniformity does not reject for any quantity at the 1% level." }` Ranks are discrete, so ties between a true rank and the posterior draws are broken at random.

# Appendix: Reproducibility {#sec-repro .appendix}

The pipeline is run with `targets::tar_make()` from the project root, after setting an API key for CollegeFootballData.com; the first full build fits all `r n_snap` weekly posteriors and the analyses of this paper and takes several hours on eight cores, and later runs fit only new weeks. `Rscript check_build.R` then verifies the store. This paper is itself a target, rendered by `tar_make()` whenever a target it reads changes; every number and figure is read from the store and nothing is refitted at render time. The analyses beyond the weekly fits (the margin-family comparison, vague-prior refits, leave-one-season-out priors, ablations, baselines, benchmark and Monte Carlo checks, the margin refits and simulation-based calibration) are targets defined in `R/07_analysis.R`, so they are rerun whenever their inputs change.

**Randomness.** Every fit uses a fixed seed (2026 for the published fits and the analyses, $1000 + i$ for the $i$-th simulation-based calibration season, and a seed per step for the replicated data and bootstraps), so a rebuild on the same data and software reproduces every number.

**Software.** R package versions are recorded in `renv.lock` at the project root; @tbl-software lists the main ones and CmdStan.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Software versions used for this render."
pk <- c("targets", "tarchetypes", "cmdstanr", "posterior", "loo", "priorsense", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "igraph")
tibble::tibble(
  Component = c("R", "CmdStan", pk),
  Version = c(paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
              tryCatch(as.character(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()), error = \(e) "--"),
              map_chr(pk, \(p) tryCatch(as.character(packageVersion(p)), error = \(e) "--")))
) |>
  ktab(align = "ll")
```

**Data.** The provider revises past data occasionally (late score corrections, reclassified games, new betting lines), so a rebuild months later need not reproduce this paper exactly. Every raw API response is cached as JSON under `data/raw/`, which is the snapshot the paper was built from; @tbl-data-hash records, for each season, what the models saw and a hash of it, so a later build can be checked against this one. This build read the data on `r format(dh$built[1], "%Y-%m-%d")`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-hash
#| tbl-cap: "The data behind this build, by season: games, completed games, games with an efficiency margin and with a closing line, and an xxHash64 hash of the season's data as the models read it."
dh |>
  transmute(Season = season, Games = fmt(games), Completed = fmt(completed), `With eff.` = fmt(with_eff),
            `With line` = fmt(with_line), Hash = paste0("\\texttt{", hash, "}")) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrl")
```
